title: Multiplying whole numbers
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: Multiplication is a fast way to add equal groups. Knowing your times tables and a few tricks makes big multiplications quick. Quick words: equal groups means sets that have the exact same number of things in each one. digit means a single number symbol like 0, 1, 2 up to 9.
To multiply, work from the right: multiply each digit, and carry to the next column when a result reaches ten or more.

steps: Tens: 6 x 3 = 18, add the carried 2 to get 20.

blocks.rule: Multiply from the right, carrying to the next column when a product reaches ten or more.

blocks.content: To multiply by 10, add one zero; to multiply by 100, add two zeros.

blocks.explain: Multiplying by 10 adds one zero: 45 becomes 450.
blocks.rule: To multiply a whole number by 10 add one zero; by 100 add two zeros.

blocks.question: To work out 12 x 25, Ann does 12 x 20 = 240, then 12 x 5 = 60, then adds: 240 + 60 = 300. Why does her method work?
options: She split 25 into 20 + 5 and multiplied each part, then added (12x20=240, 12x5=60, total 300)
It works by luck; you cannot split numbers like that
It works but the total should be 360
blocks.explain: 25 is the same as 20 + 5. Multiplying 12 by each part and adding gives the same as 12 x 25: 240 + 60 = 300. Splitting a factor into easier parts and adding the results always works.
blocks.rule: You can split a factor into parts, multiply each, and add the answers.
blocks.principle: Multiplication can be broken into parts that add back to the whole (the distributive idea).

rubric.look_for: explains that splitting a factor and adding gives the same product

misconceptions.if: multiplies the parts together instead of adding
misconceptions.coach: After splitting, add the two products (240 + 60), do not multiply them.
Use both parts: 12 x 20 AND 12 x 5.

blocks.content: Multiply column by column and carry, and use the zero trick for 10 and 100. Let's practise!
